groups.title: Capture and understand
groups.lede: Every invoice, order, receipt, contract and statement your team already receives, read into fields you can trust.

engines.name: Document reading
engines.result: Fields, line items and totals read from PDFs, scans and photos, each with the page it came from.
engines.detail: Upload by drag and drop, through the API, or from a supplier through a request link you send. Servabo reads the text (OCR for scans), classifies the document and extracts its fields. Anything it is unsure of goes to a person in the review queue, with the evidence highlighted on the page.

engines.name: Ask your documents
engines.result: Answers to questions about your documents, with a citation to the page for every claim.
engines.detail: The workspace assistant searches your own documents and answers with numbered citations you can click. It only ever reads your organization's documents.

engines.name: Table intelligence
engines.result: Tables that run across pages, rotate or lose their rules, rebuilt and checked, ready as CSV or Excel.
engines.detail: Line items, rate cards and statements are rebuilt into one table, and totals are checked against the rows so a misread figure is caught before it reaches a spreadsheet.

engines.name: Case files and bundle splitting
engines.result: A scanned bundle split into its documents, and related documents gathered into one case.
engines.detail: A 40-page scan of invoices, delivery notes and a contract is cut into separate documents automatically. Documents about the same matter are grouped, and missing ones can be requested from the sender with a link.

engines.name: Extraction memory
engines.result: Fewer corrections each month: what your reviewers fix is learned per supplier layout.
engines.detail: When a person corrects a field, Servabo learns how that layout is written. A learned rule is tried before it is trusted and withdrawn if it drifts.

groups.title: Verify and match
groups.lede: Documents checked against each other, so a wrong price, a duplicate or a changed bank account is stopped before it is paid.

engines.name: Three-way matching
engines.result: Each invoice matched to its purchase order and goods receipt, line by line, within the tolerances you set.
engines.detail: Quantities and prices are compared with what was ordered and received. A difference opens one case per invoice (copies of the same invoice are listed on it, never opened twice) for a person to approve or dispute.

engines.name: Duplicate and anomaly radar
engines.result: Duplicate invoices, changed supplier bank details and unusual amounts flagged with the evidence.
engines.detail: The radar compares every new document with your history and explains each flag in words, with the documents side by side.

engines.name: One record per supplier and customer
engines.result: Every document about the same company or person tied to one record, however its name was written.
engines.detail: "Acme Pvt Ltd", "ACME PRIVATE LIMITED" and the GSTIN on its invoices become one supplier, with every document and payment about it in one place.

engines.name: TruthMesh
engines.result: Conflicts between documents found across the whole workspace: a contract price that no invoice honours.
engines.detail: TruthMesh links documents that talk about the same thing and shows where they disagree. Ask "what if" a figure changes, and it shows which other documents it would affect.

engines.name: Document comparison
engines.result: Two to five versions of a contract or policy compared clause by clause, with a downloadable report.
engines.detail: Each clause is lined up with its counterpart in the other documents and every difference is listed in a matrix, so a changed term is never missed between drafts.

engines.name: Clause checks
engines.result: Rules your contracts must meet, checked on every new contract: a liability cap, a notice period, a governing law.
engines.detail: Write a check once as a sentence; every contract that arrives is checked against it and the result is shown with the clause it rests on.

groups.title: Track promises and obligations
groups.lede: What each document commits you to, and what it commits others to, with the date it falls due.

engines.name: Helm
engines.result: Every promise in your documents in one ledger, your rules kept true, and a plan of what to pay, hold and chase.
engines.detail: Helm is the flagship engine. You state the outcomes once (never pay above the agreed price, keep cash above a floor, pay small suppliers on time); Helm plans and checks every step against them, and a person approves.

engines.name: Obligations and deadlines
engines.result: Renewals, notice periods, payment dates and certificate expiries read from documents, with reminders.
engines.detail: Each obligation has an owner and a due date in your workspace's time zone. Reminders go out before it falls due, and a calendar feed puts them in Google or Outlook.

groups.title: Automate and post
groups.lede: The routine steps done the same way every time, and the results posted where your team already works.

engines.name: Automations
engines.result: Rules that act as documents arrive: route, tag, notify, request review or call your systems.
engines.detail: Build a rule from a trigger, conditions and actions, or install a ready workflow from the marketplace. Every run is logged with what it did and why.

engines.name: Posting to your ERP
engines.result: Approved bills, orders, receipts and journals posted to your ERP exactly once, even when a connection drops.
engines.detail: QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Business Central, SAP, NetSuite, Tally, EDI X12, UBL and SFTP. Values are mapped to your ERP's codes, and a posting that cannot be confirmed is shown as such, never sent twice.

engines.name: Batch operations
engines.result: Hundreds of documents processed, reviewed and exported together, with a package anyone can verify.
engines.detail: Exports are packaged with a manifest and SHA-256 checksums, so an auditor can prove nothing was changed after it left Servabo.

engines.name: API and webhooks
engines.result: Your own systems upload documents and receive results, with keys you scope and signed events.
engines.detail: API keys carry only the scopes you give them. Webhooks are signed, retried with backoff and shown with every delivery attempt.

engines.name: Process intelligence
engines.result: Where documents wait and why, and which ones are about to miss their deadline.
engines.detail: Servabo maps how documents actually move through your team, predicts which ones will breach their service level, and an exception agent proposes a fix: applied only when a person approves it, or within an error bound you set.

engines.name: Analytics warehouse sync
engines.result: Extracted data delivered to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks or S3 for your own reporting.
engines.detail: Choose the destination and the schedule; each delivery is recorded and can be replayed.

groups.title: Govern and audit
groups.lede: Who did what, who may do what, and where your data may go.

engines.name: Audit log
engines.result: Every sensitive change recorded with who, what and when, in a log no one can edit.
engines.detail: The database refuses to change or delete an audit entry. Keep the log for as long as you choose (at least 400 days) and export it whenever you need.

engines.name: Review together, live
engines.result: A shared review queue where everyone sees who is looking at what, with item locks and discussions.
engines.detail: Two people never decide the same item at once, and a discussion stays anchored to the paragraph it is about.

engines.name: Redaction
engines.result: Personal data removed from the page itself, not hidden behind a black box that can be lifted.
engines.detail: Names, account numbers and other identifiers are cut out of the file's image and text layer, and the redacted copy is sealed.

engines.name: Single sign-on and SCIM
engines.result: People sign in with Okta, Entra ID or Google, and joiners and leavers follow your directory.
engines.detail: SAML and OpenID Connect, a verified domain, required single sign-on and two-factor, and SCIM provisioning that respects your seats.

engines.name: Egress lockdown
engines.result: Every connection made for your organization confined to the destinations you allow.
engines.detail: Webhooks, warehouses, ERP, mail and AI providers can only reach the hosts on your list; every refusal is recorded and audited.
